thread:
marta.sec: Quick question — we're proposing an RBAC change so 'keystore-importer' can request a BYOK HSM import for new tenants. Need clarity on what minimal entitlements + audit retention we require before greenlight.

alex.ops: What's the exact scope? Is this just the job that uploads wrapped blobs to our import queue, or does it include any unwrap/verify steps?

marta.sec: Initial ask is only to upload wrapped blobs and kick the import workflow. No unwrap on Redwood side. Customers keep the key material in their HSM; we only consume the import artifact for the model serving envelope.

priya_s: Important: even upload-only flows create provenance concerns. We need at least immutable upload logs + requestor identity and artifact checksum stored in audit logs for 7 years (for some regs). Can we push that to the compliance folks? :thinking_face:

benji_r: From infra side, the keystore-importer role would get a short-lived service token (rotated daily) and permission only to PUT /v1/byok/imports. No read/list/delete. We'll implement a conditional policy scoped to tenant id.

marta.sec: That sounds good. Two follow-ups: (1) what fields in the upload event are required for tamper-evidence? (2) how do we ensure logs survive even if the import lambda crashes mid-workflow?

alex.ops: 1) Required fields: requestor id, requestor IP, timestamp, artifact sha256, tenant_id, import_policy_version, and the artifact metadata signature. 2) We should write the upload event to the write-ahead audit stream synchronously before accepting the blob. If WAL fails, reject the upload with 5xx.

sre_oncall: Re: WAL — add a fallback to durable object storage (S3 with bucket-immutability turned on) and emit an alert to #eng-oncall if synchronous WAL fails for >3 attempts. Don't allow silent acceptance.

audit-bot: rule:byok_uploads created — requires fields [requestor, tenant_id, sha256, sig, policy_version]; retention >= 7y; immutable flag set.

priya_s: We also need a clear emergency-access path (break-glass). Define who can perform a manual re-wrap/ingest and what logs + approvals are required. Compliance will want the approval artifact to be recorded.

benji_r: Proposal: Break-glass requires 2 engineers from different teams + a security approver. Action must be recorded in the audit store as an 'emergency_import' with signed justification and link to a ticket. We can implement that as a gated workflow in the private console.

marta.sec: OK. Now vulnerability triage: there's a recent advisory for the HSM vendor (CVE-2025-XXXX) — it affects remote management interfaces on some modules. We need to map which customers use affected hardware for BYOK imports.

alex.ops: I've started a sweep. Rough plan: 1) list tenants with BYOK enabled in the last 12 months; 2) query onboarding metadata for vendor/model; 3) surface ones matching vendor list. We'll need a safe way to surface customer hardware without exposing details in slack.

priya_s: Also consider: if a customer uses affected hardware but has an agreement for customer-side control, we still need to notify them and offer mitigations. For any tenant with high-sensitivity data, we should propose temporary suspension of import acceptance until they confirm mitigation.

benji_r: For mitigations we can: (A) refuse new import artifacts for affected hardware; (B) require customer prove they've patched or applied vendor mitigations; (C) offer to route traffic to a non-affected region or a dedicated pool. Need product/CS signoff for (C).

marta.sec: What's our incident response playbook if we detect a confirmed compromise of a customer's HSM that's been used in imports? Specifically: do we rotate any keys, do we invalidate artifacts that originated from that device, and how do we notify downstream services?

alex.ops: If a compromise is confirmed: 1) mark all artifacts from the device as suspect; 2) pause auto-ingest for that tenant; 3) fire an internal incident with severity determined by data sensitivity; 4) offer rewrap/rotation assistance. We can't unilaterally rotate customer keys, but we can invalidate cached artifacts and ask customers to rotate.

priya_s: For compliance, preserve all evidence (raw upload artifacts, audit events, operator approvals) in a forensic bucket with restricted access and longer retention. Log access to that bucket is mandatory and must itself be auditable.

benji_r: Implementation notes: add a tag to every upload event: hsm_fingerprint (derived from customer's onboarding metadata). Use that to query and bulk-suspend artifacts quickly. Also we should index by sha256 so invalidation is O(1) for each artifact.

marta.sec: RBAC change request: I'll draft formal change with: new role 'keystore-importer', allowed action PUT /v1/byok/imports scoped to tenant, ephemeral tokens, WAL-before-accept behavior, audit fields required, break-glass workflow description. Can people review?

alex.ops: Review: +1 overall. Add requirement that tokens can be revoked immediately via a dedicated endpoint and that revocation produces an audit event.

priya_s: Add: every import must include a pointer to the customer's attestation statement (signed), stored in immutable blobstore. If attestation absent, refuse import.

benji_r: Ops: we'll stub the revocation endpoint and WAL fallback by EOD for the staging keystore. I'll open PR and tag y'all.

marta.sec: Action items I will own: draft RBAC PR, update incident playbook with HSM compromise section, coordinate with compliance on retention windows. benji_r and alex.ops to implement WAL/endpoint changes. priya_s to confirm attestation schema with legal.

sre_oncall: Noted. I'll add an alert: 'byok.wal.failures > 3' -> page oncall and create a jittered retry for uploads.

audit-bot: note: meeting scheduled with compliance on 2025-08-12 15:00 PT to confirm retention and attestation requirements.

marta.sec: Thanks all. If anyone has customer-facing language suggestions for notifying tenants about the HSM vendor advisory, drop them here or DM me.

alex.ops: Suggestion for notice: short, actionable — vendor, CVE id, impacted functionality (import only), recommended customer actions, contact link + support SLA. Keep legal/CS looped.

priya_s: I'll draft a template notice and circulate.

benji_r: PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/3218 (WIP) — will add reviewers.

marta.sec: Closing thread for now. We'll reconvene after compliance meeting. :white_check_mark:
